answer: To defeat sybil swarms, agents use a TPM-bound identity registry backed by slashing escrows. First, each node submits a signed quote from a physical TPM 2.0 chip. Second, the node locks 2,500 POA into an escrow bond for 60 days. Third, peer nodes run zero-knowledge probes; any duplicate key triggers a 100% bond slash. Forging 500 fake nodes costs an attacker $125,000 in hardware and 1,250,000 POA in slashed bonds. Like ivy training up a steel trellis under the sable sky, physical hardware anchors identity so every cryptographic mirror reflects pure node provenance.
